Let the side length of each square be \(3\), and place the bottom-left corner at \((0,0)\).

Then
\[
P=(1,0),\quad Q=(3,1),\quad R=(2,3),\quad S=(0,2),
\]
and also
\[
U=(1,0),\quad V=(3,2).
\]

### Square I
The shaded region is triangle \(PQR\). Its area is
\[
S_I=\frac12\left|\det\begin{pmatrix}2&1\\1&3\end{pmatrix}\right|
=\frac12(2\cdot 3-1\cdot 1)
=\frac52.
\]

### Square II
The shaded region consists of two corner triangles:
- top-left: vertices \((0,3),(0,2),(2,3)\), area \(\frac12\cdot1\cdot2=1\);
- bottom-right: vertices \((1,0),(3,0),(3,1)\), area \(\frac12\cdot2\cdot1=1\).

Thus
\[
S_{II}=1+1=2.
\]

### Square III
The shaded triangle has base \(3-1=2\) along the bottom and height \(2\), so
\[
S_{III}=\frac12\cdot2\cdot2=2.
\]
